<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
The PKGBUILD only contains standard variable definitions and a source array pointing to an upstream tarball. There are no top-level command substitutions, eval, base64 decoding, curl, wget, or other downloads that would execute during `makepkg --printsrcinfo`. The sha256sums are set to a hash value but, per the gate's rules, a missing or SKIPped checksum does not affect this safety gate. The build() and package() functions are defined but not executed at this step. Hence, sourcing/parsing the PKGBUILD poses no direct malicious code execution risk.
</details>
<evidence>

All entries follow normal AUR packaging conventions: a pinned checksum, appropriate dependency declarations, and a legitimate upstream URL. No executable code, network calls, file system modifications, or obfuscation techniques are present.

Because the file contains only declarative metadata and references expected upstream sources with proper integrity checks, there is no indication of malicious injection, supply‑chain compromise, or unsafe behavior.
